links.outcome: Physician alert burden and acceptance with clinical pharmacist review of alerts
links.effect: Of 10,556 alerts, 619 went directly to physicians and 2,231 after pharmacist review; pharmacists received 17.2 alerts/day vs 7.8 notifications/day for all physicians; acceptance 89.8% (direct) and 68.4% (pharmacist-reviewed), 72.4% overall.
links.quote: Involving clinical pharmacists proved a promising approach to limit the alert burden of physicians and thus tackle alert fatigue.

links.outcome: Physician notification burden after intermediary clinical pharmacist review
links.effect: Of 10,556 alerts, 619 directly notified physicians and 2,231 notified physicians after pharmacist review. Pharmacists received 17.2 alerts per day; physicians collectively received 7.8 notifications per day.
links.quote: In 2021, a total of 10,556 alerts were generated, of which 619 triggered a direct notification to the physician and 2,231 notifications were send to the physician after evaluation by a clinical pharmacist.

links.outcome: Physician satisfaction with the deployed CDSS
links.effect: 94.5% of physicians reported being satisfied or very satisfied with the CDSS.
links.quote: In the survey, 94.5% of physicians reported being satisfied or very satisfied with the CDSS.

links.quote: On average, clinical pharmacists received 17.2 alerts per day, while all of the hospital physicians together received 7.8 notifications per day.
